newsitem.title: USA: Agribusiness group urges ADM chairman to quit.
newsitem.headline: Agribusiness group urges ADM chairman to quit.

text.p: The Agribusiness Council on Saturday urged Dwayne Andreas to resign as chairman of Archer Daniels Midland Co. after the company pleaded guilty to price fixing last week.

Nicholas Hollis, president of the nonpartisan association that helps promote U.S. agribusiness overseas, said Andreas's exit "could be the only way the scandal can be effectively put behind the company."

ADM on Thursday said Michael Andreas, vice chairman and son of Dwayne Andreas, took a temporary leave, and Terrance Wilson, a vice president in charge of corn refining, retired for medical reasons relating to progressive heart disease.
Michael Andreas and Wilson are being investigated by the Justice Department in connection with a price-fixing scheme.

On Tuesday, the Decatur, Illinois-based ADM, which calls itself the "supermarket to the world," pleaded guilty to two counts of price-fixing and agreed to pay $100 million in fines to the federal government, the largest penalty ever in a criminal antritust case.

Under the agreement, which is subject to court approval, ADM will pay $70 million to settle a charge of fixing prices for lysine, a feed additive for livestock, and $30 million in connection with citric acid, a food and beverage additive.

"This is probably just the tip of the iceberg," Hollis said in a statement. The Agribusiness Council has been investigating corruption and abuse within farm groups and other organizations with known links to ADM.
Andreas "could be spared shame and ridicule -- if not more serious problems -- by a timely resignation," Hollis said.
